site.title: Every Model
site.tagline: Every architecture since ChatGPT, side by side, from the source
site.description: How every important model architecture since ChatGPT works, from the LLaMA recipe through GQA, MoE, MLA, hybrids, sparse attention and diffusion: one workload, two landmark designs per chapter, every claim pinned to a config or a line of code.
site.author: sanjeevrg89

parts.title: The recipe everyone inherited
parts.dek: ChatGPT goes mainstream, LLaMA leaks the recipe, and every open model since cooks a variation: one decoder block, a tokenizer, a position scheme and a scale.

chapters.title: Model basics: the five ideas
chapters.question: What does a model actually compute, in plain terms?
chapters.dek: Tokens become vectors, one multiply-and-add, attention as a lookup, a volume norm, a residual edit. Ten minutes of foundations, with Qwen2.5-7B and Mistral-7B providing the real numbers.

chapters.title: One block to learn them all
chapters.question: What is the smallest piece every model since ChatGPT shares?
chapters.dek: RMSNorm, grouped-query attention and a SwiGLU feed-forward in one residual block. Qwen2.5-7B on channel A, Mistral-7B on channel B, the same token through both.

chapters.title: Words in, ids out
chapters.question: Why does one model need 32,000 words and another 201,088?
chapters.dek: Vocabularies from 32k to 201k across the roster, untied embeddings everywhere, and what the LM head costs per step.

chapters.title: Where am I in 131,072 tokens?
chapters.question: How does a model know token 100,000 comes after token 99,999?
chapters.dek: Rotary embeddings from theta 10k to 5M, YaRN extension, and the layers that stopped using positions at all.

chapters.title: Norms and gates
chapters.question: What keeps a 92-layer model trainable?
chapters.dek: RMSNorm everywhere, SwiGLU feed-forwards, and QK-norm on the attention path in Qwen3.

chapters.title: What scale costs
chapters.question: How many FLOPs does one token cost, before any cleverness?
chapters.dek: Parameter counts from 7B to 1T, two FLOPs per weight per token, and the roofline floors every later chapter reuses.

parts.title: Cheaper attention
parts.dek: The KV cache grows with every token, so a decade of attention variants competes to shrink it: share heads, shorten windows, compress latents, skip tokens.

chapters.title: Share the keys
chapters.question: Why do 28 query heads share 4 key heads?
chapters.dek: Multi-head to grouped-query attention, the repeat_kv verbatim, and KV bytes per token for every roster model.

chapters.title: Look nearby, remember far
chapters.question: What does a 4,096-token window remember about token 1?
chapters.dek: Sliding-window attention from Mistral's 4,096 to gpt-oss's 128, and which layers get the full window.

chapters.title: Compress the cache
chapters.question: How do you cache one 512-number latent instead of 128 key-value pairs?
chapters.dek: Multi-head latent attention from DeepSeek-V2-Lite to Kimi-K2: low-rank projection, decoupled RoPE, absorbed inference.

chapters.title: Attend to 2,048 of 131,072
chapters.question: Who decides which past tokens deserve full attention?
chapters.dek: DeepSeek sparse attention: a lightning indexer scores every past token and 2,048 winners get the real attention, from the V3.2 experiment to the 753B GLM-5.3 flagship.

chapters.title: Positions without embeddings
chapters.question: What happens when attention layers stop adding positions?
chapters.dek: NoPE in Kimi Linear's MLA layers and interleaved RoPE in Llama 4's iRoPE, and who carries position instead.

parts.title: Many experts
parts.dek: Capacity without the compute bill: a router wakes a few expert feed-forwards per token, from 8 coarse experts to 384 fine ones.

chapters.title: Eight experts, two awake
chapters.question: How does a 47B model cost 13B per token?
chapters.dek: Mixtral's coarse MoE: one gate, top-2 of 8 experts, and the load-balancing problem every later design answers.

chapters.title: Tiny experts
chapters.question: Why do 256 small experts beat 8 big ones?
chapters.dek: DeepSeek-V3's fine-grained MoE: 256 routed experts, 8 active, the first 3 layers dense, and what each token actually touches.

chapters.title: The expert that never sleeps
chapters.question: What does every token need, no matter the topic?
chapters.dek: The shared expert from DeepSeekMoE to V3: common knowledge in one always-on path, specialization in the routed ones.

chapters.title: The Apache MoE
chapters.question: What does the main Western open MoE do differently?
chapters.dek: gpt-oss-120B: 128 experts with 4 active, a 128-token attention window, and MoE under an Apache license.

chapters.title: Experts at scale
chapters.question: What changes when 384 experts serve 1T parameters?
chapters.dek: Kimi-K3's 896 routed experts with 16 active, plus one shared: what trillion-parameter routing looks like in the config, and keeping every rank resident.

parts.title: Beyond attention
parts.dek: Attention costs grow with the sequence, so challengers carry a fixed-size state instead: SSMs, delta rules and per-channel decays, hybridized with a little attention.

chapters.title: A state, not a cache
chapters.question: What if the past fit in a fixed-size matrix?
chapters.dek: Mamba and Mamba-2: selective state spaces, linear-time scans, and constant memory per layer.

chapters.title: Memory with a rule
chapters.question: How does a recurrent layer rewrite what it remembers?
chapters.dek: Gated DeltaNet: the delta update plus Mamba-style gating, three linear layers per attention layer.

chapters.title: A decay per channel
chapters.question: Why give every feature its own forgetting rate?
chapters.dek: Kimi-K3 runs Kimi Delta Attention at 2.8T: channel-wise decay beside NoPE MLA layers, with full attention every fourth layer of 93.

chapters.title: Seven linear, one latent
chapters.question: How far can the recurrent ratio go?
chapters.dek: MiniMax-M2.5's attention-type list: mostly Lightning attention, periodic MLA, 62 layers deep.

chapters.title: Budget every kind of state
chapters.question: How many bytes does one token leave behind in each architecture?
chapters.dek: KV, latents, recurrent states and indexer keys per token across the roster, and what 131,072 tokens need on one GPU.

parts.title: Predict more, store less
parts.dek: Once the block is set, models squeeze more tokens per pass and fewer bytes per weight: multi-token prediction, narrow formats and reasoning as architecture.

chapters.title: One pass, several tokens
chapters.question: Can one forward pass commit to more than one token?
chapters.dek: Multi-token prediction from DeepSeek-V3 training heads to GLM-5.3 and V4.1-Flash speculate-and-verify layers, and speculative decoding at serve time.

chapters.title: Fewer bits
chapters.question: How narrow can weights get before quality suffers?
chapters.dek: bf16 baselines, FP8 MoE checkpoints, MXFP4 experts in Kimi-K3: what each format stores and which kernels read it.

chapters.title: Context in memory
chapters.question: What does a full 131,072-token context weigh?
chapters.dek: State bytes at full context for all fifteen roster models, and which ones fit beside their weights on one H200.

chapters.title: Think, then answer
chapters.question: Where does reasoning live: weights, tokens or training?
chapters.dek: From o1 to R1: reasoning as post-training with RL, thinking tokens in the context, and what the architecture owes them.

parts.title: Other ways to generate
parts.dek: Not everything predicts left to right: diffusion models denoise, multimodal models fuse early, and every design still has to run somewhere.

chapters.title: Denoise, don't predict
chapters.question: What if generation refined the whole answer at once?
chapters.dek: LLaDA's masked diffusion: bidirectional attention, no KV cache, and where the speed-quality knob lives.

chapters.title: Start from a talker
chapters.question: Why initialize a diffusion model from an autoregressive one?
chapters.dek: Dream-7B's AR initialization and adaptive noise, and the commercial diffusion models that followed.

chapters.title: Early fusion
chapters.question: How do pixels become tokens the same stack can read?
chapters.dek: Natively multimodal models: early fusion in Llama 4, Kimi-K3's and V4.1-Flash's vision towers beside the text stack, and omni speech pipelines.

chapters.title: Agents and long contexts
chapters.question: Which architecture wins a 100,000-token agent loop?
chapters.dek: Agentic traffic across the roster: prefix reuse, sparse selection and linear state where it matters, with pointers into Two Engines and Two Orchestrators.

chapters.title: One engine, every architecture
chapters.question: What does each architecture ask of the engine that serves it?
chapters.dek: Kernels, expert parallelism and disaggregation per architecture family, and the flags that matter in vLLM and SGLang.

chapters.title: Field guide
chapters.question: How do you read a new model release in ten minutes?
chapters.dek: Config first, code second, paper third: the ten-minute method, the calculators in this course, and how to contribute the next architecture.
